postings.notes: Fixture row 1. 13 react-selects on the page, of which 9 are EEO/demographic and must stay untouched. Prior run evidence (applications/.../trace.jsonl): the `location` row — API field `location`, DOM id `candidate-location`, a Pelias autocomplete with no fixed option list — failed twice with `no_options_rendered` and ended as an `ask`; the `resume` upload failed once with `file_input_not_found`. Both are the regressions this bench must catch. `#country` is a separate react-select that drives the intl-tel-input `#phone`.

postings.notes: Fixture row 2 and the smallest form in the set — 8 rows, all required, no section headings. Two Ashby Booleans render as a `button[data-option]` Yes/No pair over a hidden checkbox. Prior smoke run failed one of them with `not_boolean: Maybe`, i.e. the adapter is correct and the *answer* was out of vocabulary; the bench should score that as an `ask`, not an adapter bug.

Expect this row to fail until a date path exists; that failure is the measurement. Also a 2-option required checkbox group (relocation/entity), a GDPR retention consent classified `policy_gate` (must stay an `ask`), and a "Which pronouns…" *text* row classified `sensitive` that must stay empty.

This is exactly where react-select's substring filtering bites — src/browser/adapters/greenhouse.mjs types the first 24 normalized characters and then matches by label, so a value like "New York" must not land on "New York (excluding New York City)". 25 rows, the second-longest form here.

postings.notes: Hardest row: 28 questions, 17 required, four sections (Links / Application Questions / Accommodations / Screening Questions). Carries a 24-option ValueSelect ("What brought you to this job posting") which per src/schema/ashby.mjs:21 should render as 24 radio inputs — whether Ashby switches to a dropdown at that length is unverified and is one of the things this row measures [INFERENCE]. Two one-option MultiValueSelects (a conditional-offer acknowledgement, required, and a marketing opt-in, optional) hit the same single-checkbox branch as row 7. Three required essays plus a `why_us`, so the writer path runs at full width. Two rows classified `sensitive` by label ("Pronouns", an accommodations textarea) must stay untouched. The two AI-topic essays are questions *about* AI tooling, not AI-usage attestations — the form carries no attestation and no login.
